# ethereum-optimism/design-docs Monthly Report (June 2026)

## 🚀 Highlights
In June 2026, development focused heavily on hardening the infrastructure for interoperability (interop) and refining node synchronization stability. Significant progress was made in resolving critical deadlocks within the `op-reth` execution layer and establishing recovery protocols for invalid interop messages. The month also saw a shift toward long-running devnet environments and the implementation of protocol-level safeguards, such as sequencer refund limits and enhanced observability for failsafe states.

## 🛠️ Key Developments

### Protocol Security & Documentation
Efforts were directed toward documenting edge cases in network behavior and ensuring protocol stability during hardforks.
*   **Hardfork Safety:** Added critical warnings to the generic hardfork Failure Mode Analysis (FMA) documentation regarding potential chain splits involving `rbuilder` [#386](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/pull/386).
*   **Guardian Permissions:** Concluded the design review process for improved Guardian permission proposals, finalizing the architectural direction for these security roles [#169](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/169).

### Node Performance & Synchronization
Substantial work went into debugging complex synchronization issues between the Consensus Layer (CL) and Execution Layer (EL).
*   **CL Sync Recovery:** Resolved a major issue where `op-supernode`/`op-reth` synchronization would stall due to missing blocks. The team identified a cyclic deadlock in the `StateTrieOverlayManager` caused by holding locks across `rayon` compute operations. Two patches were developed to ensure locks are released during blocking computations, successfully allowing test chains to sync without "wedging" [#21076](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/21076).
*   **REVM Integration:** Established a strategy to maintain synchronization with `revm` releases (specifically v111), focusing on shared type definitions and support for the upcoming Amsterdam hardfork [#21069](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/21069).

## 🐛 Issues & Triage

### New & Active Issues
*   **Interop Recovery & Failsafes:** A primary focus emerged around handling invalid interop messages. A new runbook is being developed to manage chain reorgs and failsafe triggers [#21161](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/21161). This follows observations that the `op-reth` transaction pool fails to resume after a failsafe is disabled without a full restart of both the node and the `op-rbuilder` [#21149](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/21149).
*   **Sequencer Refund Limits:** Discussions are ongoing regarding a protocol-level cap on sequencer rebates. The proposed solution involves enforcing a `MAX_GAS_LIMIT` to prevent excessive computation during the refund process [#20709](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/20709).
*   **Testing Infrastructure:** The team is investigating intermittent timeouts in the `op-e2e-fuzz` CI jobs [#21191](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/21191). Additionally, tests for `relayMessage` gas changes remain pending a stable Foundry release that supports isolated EVM environments [#14609](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/14609).

### Closed Issues
*   **Design Reviews:** The design review for Guardian permissions was successfully closed, moving the proposal toward implementation [#169](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/169).

## 💬 Community & Collaboration
The month was characterized by high-intensity technical troubleshooting between maintainers, particularly regarding the `op-reth` and `op-supernode` stack. Collaboration was evident in the rapid remediation of the `interop-bench-3` environment, where developers identified that a simple node restart was insufficient to restore the transaction pool, leading to the proposal of a new `failsafe-state` gauge metric [#21151](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/21151) for better observability. The transition from local devnets to long-running devnets indicates a maturing phase of the current development cycle.
